angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 500,904 km at 180.73 pc = 0.04 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 5.5330 +/- 0.0097 mas (same row, RUWE 1.04): 180.73 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.72 +/- 0.018 solar radii from Reller et al. 2026, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-4409 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026A&A...712A.142R/abstract): 500,904 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.763 +/- 0.026 solar masses from Reller et al. 2026, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-4409 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026A&A...712A.142R/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4928 +/- 47 K from Reller et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-4409 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026A&A...712A.142R/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Reller et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-4409 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026A&A...712A.142R/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-4409.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.606, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-4409 (pscomppars): spectral type K, from Reller et al. 2026 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026A&A...712A.142R/abstract)

luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-4409 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -0.56976, from Reller et al. 2026 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026A&A...712A.142R/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-4409 (pscomppars): age 7 Gyr, from Reller et al. 2026 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026A&A...712A.142R/abstract)
